questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I am leaning the language, so I wanted to go to where I would be forced to use the language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. If there was anything else, I could ask.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Orientation, help with opening bank account, help joining elective courses

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Get a hostel and arrive a bit (days/a week) before orientation and just walk down the streets near campus and see if there’s places with “租” in big letters on a paper glued to the door or wall, and then translate with google translate or look up the name of the place to see if they have a Line or a physical office location. You can go talk with them about renting and can often rent from whenever to whenever.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Higher price, but also more freedom. You probably have to get deposit back in cash from a different place as they probably won’t be able to return the money to a foreign bank account.
There’s often no kitchen, but there will be furnished options.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: 5 for courses at the CLC (Chinese Language Center), and 3 for the rest of the university.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
For courses in the CLC (Chinese Language Center) I was already enrolled in the class I was supposed to take, but we also had the option of responding to a survey, confirming by email and then paying at the administration for short elective classes.

For courses at the regular university you have to sign up online, email the professor to get approval of joining, get a signature from the professor and handing that in to the administration to process you into the class.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It is possible to contact the administration of the different departments and the OIR (office of international relations) to get help registering for the different classes. For the electives at the CLC (Chinese language center) however, you should contact the CLC administration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Yes, but there was also more exciting classes in the morning time, that overlapped with my other classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are going for chinese language learning, don’t take electives or only do one of the CLC one’s.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took B102 Chinese

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It is definitely Language learning. We did not practice writing that much, but read a lot out loud, both in a group at the same time and alone.
The teachers at the CLC (Chinese Language Center) were also helpful with explaining practical things; eg. If someone got a tooth ache and had to see a dentist or if you were curious about chinese medicine or where to buy gifts and what to get that is culturally different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: “B102: intermediate Chinese” and “Taiwanese”

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The chinese courses and if you are curious and ready to learn something completely different at the same time the the taiwanese elective course at the CLC as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You have to ask to know about them. They have a website all in chinese (you can use a chrome extension to translate or use the camera in the google translate app to translate)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Various instrument clubs i.e. Guzheng or modern band instruments, Hanfu club, yoga, hiking, basketball, dj-ing and many more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Guzheng classes; it is something culturally unique and the teacher also spoke english.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Join the OIR’s and CLC’s field trips, they make you experience things you probably didn’t realize existed.
You can also go to rainbow village, the skyscraper malls, the Taiwan national comics museum and/or anime lane in the same city and/or go to “sun moon lake” and “jiu fen olde street” a bit further away.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: If you have google translate it is a bit easier communication wise, but it was otherwise pretty ok adjusting.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you are able to speak chinese it is easier, but joining the english language club events is also a great opportunity.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You sometimes don’t get a lot of information or get information a bit later.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Prompt responses. If you send an email you could sometimes get a reply within half an hour. The longest wait is typically 1 weekday and 2 at most. But usually you get a reply within the day

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don’t be afraid to ask if you are unsure of something.
Arrive a bit earlier and find apartment if you want to live off campus.
Enjoy your time and take things as they come.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Taiwan has a national receipt lottery so look that one up and save your receipts.
Doing the health check in taiwan is cheaper and less bureaucratic than in Denamrk. Ask the contact person you get at Tunghai if it is possible to do a make-up one in Taiwan if you don’t mind getting checked  and getting blood drawn in an office with a lot of other people around.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Language, new friends, and learning to advocate for one self

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not getting enough information or suddenly having to do send signed papers to different places

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
